questions.question_text: Describe Rama Natha's transformation in 'A Bottle of Dew'. How did Sage Mahipati guide him?
questions.model_answer: Initially, Rama Natha was a lazy, gullible landowner who neglected his fields searching for a gold-making potion. Sage Mahipati cleverly instructed him to collect five litres of morning dew from banana trees planted by his own hands. Over six years, Rama Natha worked tirelessly to build a vast plantation. When the dew failed to turn copper into gold, the sage showed him gold coins earned from selling the bananas. Realizing that honest labor was the true source of wealth, Rama Natha became a dedicated farmer.

questions.question_text: Write a reflective paragraph on 'Hard Work vs Shortcuts to Success' based on 'A Bottle of Dew'.
questions.model_answer: Many people seek shortcuts to wealth, but true success comes only through dedicated effort. In 'A Bottle of Dew', Rama Natha wasted time seeking a magic potion until Sage Mahipati redirected him to farming. Through six years of labor, he built a prosperous plantation. Real success requires patience and persistent work; shortcuts lead to delusion, whereas honest labor brings lasting fulfillment.
value_points: Contrast magic shortcuts with physical labor
Conclude with moral lesson on self-reliance

questions.question_text: How does Jean de la Fontaine highlight the theme of vanity in 'The Raven and the Fox'?
questions.model_answer: The poet depicts Mr. Raven holding a valuable morsel of food. Rather than enjoying his meal silently, his desire for admiration makes him vulnerable. When Reynard the Fox lavishes fake praise on his plumage and sweet voice, the Raven succumbs completely. Eager to prove his artistic greatness and be hailed 'King of the Woods', he opens his beak, causing the morsel to drop. The fable vividly shows how vanity blinds reason.

questions.question_text: Write a short paragraph on 'Why We Should Beware of Flattery'.
questions.model_answer: Flattery is insincere praise used to manipulate others for personal gain. Unlike honest appreciation, flatterers appeal to our vanity to weaken our judgment. As shown in 'The Raven and the Fox', accepting false compliments can lead to embarrassing losses. We must cultivate self-awareness and remain cautious when showered with exaggerated praise.
